name: Decimen Optical Transfer
tagline: Send a file between two devices using nothing but a screen and a camera — data travels as light
description: Decimen Optical Transfer moves files across an air gap using only a screen and a camera: one page renders the file as an endless stream of animated QR codes, and a second device points its camera at it to reconstruct the file. There is no network path, no app, no pairing, and no permissions beyond the camera — the payload literally travels as light, and it works offline after the first visit. Because a screen-to-camera link has no back-channel, the sender streams fountain-coded (Luby transform) frames so the receiver can collect any ~K·1.15 distinct frames in any order and peel the file out — dropped frames cost time, never correctness. Built with node-qrcode and a custom zxing-cpp build, it reaches sustained screen-to-camera throughput of around 418.5 KB/s, and the interface is localized into twelve languages. TypeScript, currently at 5.7k stars.
highlights: Air-gapped file transfer through pure screen-to-camera optical streaming — no network path between devices
Fountain-coded (Luby transform) frames let the receiver rebuild the file from any ~K·1.15 distinct frames in any order
Measured ~418.5 KB/s sustained screen-to-camera throughput with per-transfer diagnostics reports
Works offline after first visit and installs as an app on iOS and Android
Twelve-language UI with right-to-left layout, built on node-qrcode and a custom zxing-cpp build
curatorNote: The no-back-channel + fountain-code design is a genuinely elegant answer to the 'no network' constraint. Watching a phone pull a file out of the air at 130 KB/s is the kind of demo that makes this worth starring.
